subject: Unexpected charges attributed to service-account after key rotation
messages:
From: Anjali Rao <anjali@liftapp.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden postpay charges — please investigate

Hi Laura,

We just received our October invoice and there is a ~$4,800 line item labelled "postpay: ingest service-account" covering Oct 1–3. We did a quick check on our side and don't see any intentional backfills or big traffic changes. Attached is a CSV export from our internal telemetry (liftapp_usage_oct3.csv) plus the invoice PDF.

A few quick facts:
- Account: LiftApp (account id: LIFT-9983)
- Invoice: INV-20261001
- We rotate API keys nightly; there was a rotation on Oct 1 at 00:05 UTC.

Can you confirm whether these events were attributed to our production service account or to a staging key? If this is an attribution issue we need the usage traces to reconcile with our finance team — we've put the invoice on hold for now.

Thanks,
Anjali Rao
Head of Platform Operations
LiftApp

Attachments: liftapp_usage_oct3.csv, invoice_20261001.pdf

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@liftapp.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden postpay charges — please investigate

Hi Anjali — thanks for the quick report and the files. We're looking into this now.

Next steps from our side:
- Ben (billing/instrumentation) will pull the per-request attribution for Oct 1–3 and check whether two API keys mapped to the same org_id after your rotation.
- Marissa (operations) will validate any backfill/reprocess jobs on the ingestion side.

If we find an internal attribution error we'll propose a provisional credit so you can clear the hold. Can you confirm the preferred contact for a formal credit memo (billing@liftapp.com vs your AP team)? Also, if you have a short-lived op-key we should exclude during our analysis, please send it.

I'll follow up with a timeline once Ben has the first pass of logs (should be within 4 business hours).

—Laura
Laura Bennett
Account Manager, Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: proposed-credit-20261005.pdf (draft)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-04T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden postpay charges — please investigate

Laura / Marissa — quick technical findings from the first pass:

1) Attribution trace: there are two distinct api_key hashes seen in our ingestion logs for LIFT-9983 between 2026-10-01T00:00Z and 2026-10-03T23:59Z. One hash maps cleanly to their production key (api_key-prod-xxxx). The other resolves to a service-account that shares the same org_id (LIFT-9983) but is tagged "sa-rotation-temp" in their metadata.

2) Root cause suspect: when LiftApp rotated keys at 2026-10-01T00:05Z, some of their ephemeral service-account tokens were minted with an incorrect tenant header (X-Org-Id) due to a client-side config that was still pointing at a staging DNS alias. As a result, ingestion from those ephemeral tokens got attributed to the production org_id.

3) Evidence: I've attached a short extract to the drive link (drive.redwood/prod/forensic/liftapp-rotation-logs) and included sample request ids: rqd_2a9f3e, rqd_2a9f3f, rqd_2a9f40 that show identical payloads but different key hashes.

4) Quantity & cost impact: approximately 3.9M tokens were attributed to the prod org across Oct 1–3, which matches the invoice delta.

Immediate recommendations:
- We perform a manual re-attribution for the affected request ids (surgical reassign to their staging tenant).
- Issue a provisional credit for the disputed amount while we complete the re-attribution and a short postmortem.

I'll start a reprocessing job now in a limited window; it should complete within 12 hours. If confirmed, we'll push the credit and a corrected invoice.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Billing & Instrumentation
ben_carter@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Anjali Rao <anjali@liftapp.com>, billing@liftapp.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden postpay charges — please investigate

Hi Anjali / LiftApp billing team — quick update and plan: 

Summary: Ben's preliminary analysis shows ingestion events from ephemeral tokens minted during your Oct 1 rotation were attributed to your production org_id due to a tenant header misconfiguration on some clients. We've started a targeted re-attribution for the ~3.9M tokens and will reconcile the invoice after the job completes.

What we will do now (timeline):
- 08:15 — re-attribution job queued (non-destructive; only metadata reassign).
- 12:00 — job expected to finish; Ben will validate sample request ids and produce an evidence bundle.
- 13:00 — if re-attribution confirmed, Redwood will issue a provisional credit equal to the disputed line and generate a corrected invoice. A draft credit memo is attached for your review (proposed-credit-20261005.pdf).

Requested from LiftApp:
- Please confirm the AP contact for the credit memo (billing@liftapp.com is fine if that's the correct mailbox).
- Would you like us to auto-block ingestion from the suspect key hashes while you fix the client DNS/config? We can enforce a temporary hold to avoid repeat events.

We'll keep the invoice on hold pending completion; if anything changes I'll escalate immediately. Sorry for the disruption and we'll include a short postmortem when done.

Thanks,
Laura

--
Attachment: proposed-credit-20261005.pdf

From: Anjali Rao <anjali@liftapp.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: billing@liftapp.com
Date: 2026-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden postpay charges — please investigate

Thanks Laura / Ben — that plan works for us. billing@liftapp.com confirms they are the AP contact. Please go ahead with the re-attribution and provisional credit; we'll patch the client DNS immediately and share confirmation when done. Appreciate the fast turnaround.

—Anjali
Anjali Rao
Head of Platform Operations, LiftApp
